bug_semantics: The authenticated POST /company/save path accepted a company-logo upload without any server-side type, extension, content, or size validation, derived the stored suffix from UploadedFile::extension(), and wrote the bytes into a web-public location. An attacker with both create-company and update-company permissions could therefore upload an SVG containing an embedded <script>; direct navigation to the static logo URL executed attacker JavaScript in the application origin, including for an unauthenticated visitor.
flaw_origin: dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c first implemented custom company logos in app/Http/Controllers/CompanyController.php and resources/views/company/company.blade.php. It added a multipart file input that explicitly admitted SVG and copied the uploaded bytes under public/asset/upload/company using the content-derived extension, with no server-side allow-list or content sanitization. Later controller extraction/refactoring preserved the unsafe upload, and 4c15d20a57c4225bb3853bad2c5b01b3da11121f changed the destination to Laravel's public disk without adding validation; those later changes are not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, has the single subject 'Company custom logo.', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The first-party Secur0 CNA record at https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-78337-unrestricted-upload-company-logo-svg-xss identifies CompanySaveController::save(), POST /company/save, versions before 5.15.13, public /storage/company/{slug}/{file} delivery, BIC dbd8f149, and patch aaa4fc76. `git show dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows the original server-side block taking `$request->file('logo')->extension()` and copying the unvalidated file into `public/asset/upload/company/...`; the same commit makes the form multipart and adds a logo file input whose accept list includes image/svg. `git log 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca -L 41,49:app/Http/Controllers/Company/CompanySaveController.php` traces the upload lineage through later refactors back to dbd8f149, while showing that 4c15d20 only replaced the copy with `storeAs(..., 'public')`. Direct parent-tree verification with `git show 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055:app/Http/Controllers/CompanyController.php` shows save() ending after scalar company fields with no logo/file handling, and the parent company form has neither multipart encoding nor a logo input. At the vulnerable fix parent, routes/module/company.php maps POST /company/save with create-company and update-company gates, and config/filesystems.php maps the public disk to storage/app/public with public/storage as its link. `git tag --contains dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` returns all published tags v1.0.0, v2.0.1, v4.6.0, v5.5.3, and v5.14.0. `git tag --contains aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17` returns no tag; the fix changes version.php from 5.15.12 to 5.15.13. `git show aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17` directly replaces the unvalidated Request path with CompanySaveRequest validation and ValidateSafeSvg, rejecting script tags, event handlers, javascript: URLs, iframe/object/embed content, and oversized or disallowed logo types. `git cat-file commit dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` proves a one-parent, human-authored BIC with no AI marker.
reasoning: The disclosed flaw is not merely the 2026 switch to Laravel's public disk: the security boundary was already absent when custom logos were first introduced in 2022. The smallest causal commit is dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c because it first created both the upload entry point and the unchecked public write, and line history shows later commits only moved or rewrote that same unsafe mechanism. Its immediate parent 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055 has no logo upload in either the save controller or company form, establishing parent absence. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent commit, so there is no squash to decompose. It predates every repository release tag, whereas the direct advisory patch aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17 bumps the application boundary from 5.15.12 to 5.15.13 and is present only on post-tag branches, matching the affected-before-5.15.13 advisory boundary. Finally, attribution is based only on the raw BIC commit object: both identities are Gustavo Novaro and there is no AI co-author, generator trailer, or bot marker. Therefore the causal BIC is human-authored and the closed verdict is NOT_AI; AI metadata on any later refactor or fix is irrelevant to BIC attribution.
